primary_claim: Semantic step clustering compresses a collection of 1,000 chains of thought on a fixed prompt into a graph roughly 35x smaller than the raw traces, and this compressed graph has predictive power for a model's downstream output correctness that outperforms no-clustering baselines and matches a Gemini-with-sample-rollouts baseline.

effect.value: current method has the lowest mean RMSE across 6 test prompts, considerably outperforms no-clustering baselines and the no-rollout Gemini baseline, and performs similarly to the Gemini baseline given 20 sample rollouts

stated_future_work: More research effort should go into studying many chains of thought collectively and identifying global patterns
Finding downstream tasks to test methods against is a priority
Develop methods that sit between the two extremes of the granularity/supervision axes (semantic clustering is fine and unsupervised, algorithmic clustering is coarse and supervised)
Excited for future work building on this methodology or developing new approaches to studying global CoT
limitations_stated: Not confident that the chosen abstractions are the 'right' way to think about global chains of thought
Raw embedding visualizations of the semantic graph do not exhibit any obvious structure and are provided only for context
Manual inspection of clusters still finds occasional poor clusters
None of the predictive methods perform very well in absolute terms, as shown by comparison to a 50%-constant baseline
Prompts are limited to math problems where clear reasoning structure is expected
quote: We find that our graph has some predictive power—preliminary evidence that compressing CoTs into a sequence of clusters using our method captures nontrivial structure.
